Anil Mehta

Hi Anil / team — Vivek here from Redwood Security. Below is a brief threat-model and trust-zone summary you can include in your packet. I attached a machine-readable trust_zones_matrix.xlsx and our SOC summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) for evidence.

Summary (tl;dr): Redwood provides multi-layer tenant isolation across control and data planes, default-deny egress controls per deployment, and configurable private deployment options (VPC, VPC peering, dedicated GPU pools) to eliminate public egress where required. Key mitigations address cross-tenant inference data leakage, unauthorized model exfiltration, and privileged-control-plane abuse.

Trust zones and controls (high level):
- Control Plane (Redwood-managed, SaaS-hosted):
  - Purpose: API tokens, account/route orchestration, usage analytics.
  - Isolation: Logical separation from customer inference data; access limited by least privilege and mutual TLS.
  - Mitigations: RBAC, audit logs, mTLS between services, HSM/KMS for secret management.

- Data Plane (Customer workload; Hosted / Dedicated / Private):
  - Purpose: Model serving, KV cache, request decoding, tokenization.
  - Isolation Modes:
    - Hosted: Shared multi-tenant GPU pools with strict per-tenant process and memory isolation, prefix-KV caching scoped to tenant, automatic rate-limiting.
    - Dedicated: Customer-dedicated GPU pools, network filtered egress, private routing to customer-controlled VPCs.
    - Private (VPC / On-prem): Customer-managed network boundaries, no public internet egress by default.
  - Mitigations: Kernel/address-space isolation, per-tenant filesystem and cache namespaces, continuous batching policies with enforced quotas.

Egress and third-party routing:
- Default behavior: customer traffic is routed only to approved outbound hosts; third-party API calls (e.g., embeddings providers) are blocked by default in Private/Dedicated modes and allowed only with explicit policy and audit.
- Configurability: Customers can define egress allowlists and per-route fallbacks (internal+regional model variants).
- Monitoring: Token-level telemetry and per-route traces recorded for audit; anomalous outbound flows trigger alerts.

Threat model highlights (attack surfaces & mitigations):
- Lateral tenant access: mitigated by strict process-level isolation, KV cache scoping, ephemeral per-request identities.
- Model/weights exfiltration via side-channel: mitigations include quantization fingerprinting, telemetry-based anomaly detection, and rate-throttling for bulk token access patterns.
- Control-plane compromise: limited blast radius via role separation, per-tenant keys, and automated rotation via KMS/HSM.
- Compromised customer keys: support for external KMS and HSM-backed key storage to prevent server-side exposure.

Deliverables attached: trust_zones_matrix.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf. We can also provide an annotated network export with explicit firewall rules if you need it for procurement.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachments: trust_zones_matrix.xlsx; redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Thanks Vivek — that's useful. Couple of follow-ups for our architecture reviewers:

1) In Dedicated mode, can you provide standard firewall rules or an Iptables-like export for the egress allowlist? Our network team wants exact ports/hosts to pre-approve.
2) For Private (VPC) options: do you support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink? If so, is mutual TLS still enforced between our VPC and Redwood data plane?
3) We have a small set of embeddings calls that must go to a vendor in eu-west-1. How do you support region-restricted third-party integration for a tenant that otherwise is in us-west-2?

If you can reply quickly with those three items, procurement can move the packet forward.

Regards,
Anil

--

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFI: network topology, egress controls & trust-zone summary

Hi Anil — quick answers below, and happy to provide a firewall ruleset export and a short runbook for your network ops team.

1) Dedicated firewall rules: yes — we can produce an explicit ruleset that includes port ranges, destination CIDRs, and DNS entries. Typical Allowed Egress (example):
   - TCP 443 to approved hostnames (SNI-based allowlist)
   - NTP outbound only to approved time servers
   - Internal control-plane signaling over mTLS on ephemeral ports (documented in the export)
We will attach an iptables-style manifest you can import to a perimeter firewall for Dedicated nodes.

2) Private deployment connectivity: we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for Private and Dedicated deployments. Mutual TLS is preserved end-to-end between customer VPC endpoints and Redwood data plane sidecars; certs are managed via KMS/HSM integration and we rotate them on a customer-configurable cadence.

3) Region-restricted third-party integrations: we support per-tenant routing policies. For your case we can pin embeddings calls to eu-west-1 instances while keeping inference serving in us-west-2 — the routing layer enforces egress only to the eu-west-1 vendor endpoints for those routes and logs them for audit. For Private deployments we can also provide a regional proxy inside your VPC to control egress locality.

Action items:
- We'll produce an iptables-style firewall manifest and a short runbook by EOD tomorrow.
- Aditya will share the drive link with the procurement packet and SOC summary.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
